SparkR does not work right after sparkR.init(). Keeps reporting Error "Lost an executor"
Issue Type: Bug
Assignee: Unassigned
Attachments: ErrorSnapshop.PNG, slaveUI.PNG
Created: 23/Feb/15 7:09 PM
Environment:

AWS, sequenceiq/docker-spark, SparkR
Priority: Major
Reporter: XW Gong

I have a AWS instance and am running the sequenceiq/docker-spark (including hadoop and spark) on it. The R and SparkR were installed on AWS.

After I initiated a spark context using the following command:
sc <- sparkR.init(master='spark://ip-10-64-65-168:7077', appName="ER")

The connect was built successfully. But the error messages popped up soon. The main line of the message is: "ERROR TaskSchedulerImpl: Lost an executor 0 (already removed): remote Akka client disassociated". And the same error messages will repeat for executor 1, 2, ....

I am new to spark, and I have done online research for a few weeks, but still could not fix it. Any ideas or hints will be appreciated very much! Thanks!!!

Attached pictures are the screen snapshop of the terminal and the slave UI page. And the stderr Log from one of the Executor is as follows:

Re: SparkR does not work right after sparkR.init(). Keeps reporting Error "Lost an executor"

Hi Shivaram,

Thanks for your quick tips. It seems that the error was fixed. (Please go to the bottom for my new questions, thanks!)

Here are what I did:
In the first trial, I downloaded the SparkR-pkg from Github, and run the following command:
SPARK_VERSION=1.2.0 ./install-dev.sh
Then I found that the SparkR package was installed into the /lib directory of SparkR-pkg, NOT into the R library directory. I was not sure if I could copy it to the R library directory directly. So I tried the other way.

In the 2nd trial, I edited the build.sbt file under /pkg/src/, changed the value of defaultSparkVersion to 1.2.0. Then I used "R CMD build" to create a R source package file SparkR_0.1.tar.gz. Then in the R shell, I installed the SparkR from the source package file.

After that, I can ran the sparkcontext instantiation line without the "lost executors" errors.

**************************************New question****************************************
1) I created the SparkContext using the following command:
sc <- sparkR.init(master='spark://ip-10-64-65-168:7077',appName='ER_test',sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory='10g',spark.num.executors='4',spark.executor.cores='1'))

I expected to see 4 executors. But on the slave webUI, I always see only ONE executor 0, even when I submitted some testing example, such as wordcount.

Any idea?

2) When I ran the wordcount example, I got the similar error message as in the post-173 (https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-173). I followed your comment in the post to change the hadoop version.

What I did is similar to the above. That is, edited build.sbt and changed the defaultHadoopVersion to 2.6.0. Then rebuilt the SparkR package.

After that, when I instantiated sparkContext, I got a WARN message: "NativeCodeLoader: Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable."

Is it OK?

Thanks again for your kind and generous help!!!!!!

Re: SparkR does not work right after sparkR.init(). Keeps reporting Error "Lost an executor"

1) Is there a reason why you are passing flags like spark.executor.cores=1 and spark.num.executors ? I am not sure what the flags do but I don't think you need this for a simple EC2 cluster. Also the image attached shows that 1 executor is running on 1 slave machine. The executor though has 8 cores (or 8 slots) to run tasks i.e. you can run 8 tasks in parallel. This is default behavior for Spark where it runs one executor which uses all the cores. Just curious: How many slave machines are there in your cluster ?

2) The HDFS warnings can be ignored (they refer to some native libraries which only matter for things like LZO compression etc.)
